instruction:
Custom attribute dictionary from CSV

Attach a SketchUp `AttributeDictionary` named `"PricingData"` to every ComponentDefinition in `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\products.dae`, populating each dictionary from the matching row of `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\prices.csv`, then export the result to `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.dae`. Store the AttributeDictionary values either inside the DAE or in an optional sidecar JSON file.

Inputs:
- `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\products.dae` - contains 10 component definitions named `Prod_001`, `Prod_002`,..., `Prod_010`. Each definition is a closed axis-aligned box (real geometry) instantiated in the scene. The per-component name appears both as the `name` attribute of the `<geometry>` element and as the `name` attribute on its scene `<node>`.
- `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\prices.csv` - 10 rows with columns `name, cost_usd, material_id, supplier`. Each row's `name` matches exactly one ComponentDefinition in `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\products.dae`.

Operation (matches `[SU-Ruby] ComponentDefinition#attribute_dictionary`):
For each ComponentDefinition `<ProdName>`, set `AttributeDictionary("PricingData")` with three keys drawn from the CSV row:
cost_usd -> Float (e.g. 12.5)
material_id -> Integer (e.g. 7)
supplier -> String (e.g. "Acme Industrial")
Types must be preserved: `cost_usd` is a real number, `material_id` is an integer, `supplier` is a string (not quoted, not coerced to int if it happens to look numeric).

Serialize the AttributeDictionary using EITHER of the following (at least one is mandatory):
(a) A `<extra>` element inside each `<geometry>` (ComponentDefinition) or inside each scene `<node>` that instantiates it, containing `<technique profile="SketchUp">` wrapping `<attribute_dictionary name="PricingData">` with three `<attribute name="..." type="...">VALUE<\attribute>` children. Recognised type hints: `int`, `float`, `bool`, `string`.
(b) A sibling file `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\attributes.json` placed next to `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.dae`, mapping each component name to its three-key dictionary:
{
"Prod_001": {"cost_usd": 12.5, "material_id": 7, "supplier": "Acme"},...
}
If both are present, their values must agree exactly.

Units \ axes: unchanged from the input DAE (meters, Z-up). Geometry must round-trip: same 10 component definitions, same vertex counts, same scene instantiations.

Write the DAE to `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.dae`. If you use the sidecar route (b), also write `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\attributes.json` to the same directory.

Requirements:
1. `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.dae` exists and parses as well-formed XML \ COLLADA.
2. The DAE contains exactly 10 ComponentDefinitions (geometries) named `Prod_001`..`Prod_010`.
3. An `AttributeDictionary` named `PricingData` is present for all 10 components, either (a) as a `<extra>\<technique profile="SketchUp">\<attribute_dictionary name="PricingData">` block inside the DAE (attached to the `<geometry>` or its scene `<node>`), or (b) as an `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\attributes.json` file in the same directory with 10 entries keyed by component name.
4. Each `PricingData` dictionary contains exactly the three keys `cost_usd`, `material_id`, `supplier`.
5. `cost_usd` matches the CSV row within 1e-3 (float).
6. `material_id` matches the CSV row exactly (integer - must NOT be a float).
7. `supplier` matches the CSV row exactly (string - not stripped, not quoted).
8. If both the DAE `<extra>` block and `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\attributes.json` are present, their values agree for every component.
